sourceNotes.11.275–290: Wheat tables. Recovered converted column for 1423–1451, kept 1551 converted quotation at 2s and corrected year 1557. 1288 eight prices average 2s 7¼d; Smith’s printed number is disclosed alongside the data. For 1339–1416 printed total exceeds sum of annual figures by 2d; exact mean from printed total £1 5s 9⅓d. For 1499–1560 mean 10s 5/24d. Cambridge 1637–1700 mean £2 11s ⅓d.
sourceNotes.23.23,23.25: Both Amsterdam bank tables retain prices for metal and money, including fractional values.
sourceNotes.25.76: Tariff schedule retained row by row in both editions.
sourceNotes.25.30–35 / 29.57–71: Cannan volume II and main-text cross-check: 1771 bounty £2,085; 1774 248 vessels, bounty £16,952 2s 6d; 1777 43,313 barrels caught; 1781 £9,613 12s 6d. Eleven rows independently sum to all four stated totals. Annual salt averages use 936,974 and 168,226 bushels divided by 11. Converting 378,347 loose barrels at 3:2 gives 252,231⅓. Smith reports exceptionally high per-barrel 1759 figures in both text witnesses; distinguish his report from our calculations.
sourceNotes.31.202–205: Totals for malt, beer and ale duties reconcile to £2,595,853 plus fractional shillings and pence.
sourceNotes.32.48–50: Two French remittances are the proceeds of prizes (captured property) and a settlement for prisoners; both sums retain pounds, shillings and pence.
